Checked as the reporter on candidate sha256:33266ccd (source 152db5b51). The repair is a disclosure only: D-282 in docs/delivery/decisions.md says the release notes and 25 register rows cite old-branch findings F-DG7-913…971, whose records are at 1612f85fc, that 'validate --stage DG7 here cannot show them' and that 'they are not findings of this gate'. Nothing that the finding named changed (log 79): requirements.csv and docs/handover/release-notes.md are byte-identical to the round-1 candidate; the same 25 rows still cite 14 F-DG7-9xx ids and none of them qualifies the ids (no 1612f85fc, 'old branch' or D-282); no docs/handover file mentions 1612f85fc or D-282; findings.json on this branch holds no F-DG7-9xx id. The finding expected both (a) cited ids to resolve or be qualified where they are cited, and (b) each completes-after-gate clause to name a condition the DG7 gate on this branch can show. (b) is still contradicted: the REQ-DLV-014 later clause in the register and release-notes.md l.36 still reads 'with each DG7 finding (round 2: 915, 935, 960-963) fixed and verified by a non-owner, shown by validate.mjs --stage DG7 at the gate', which D-282 itself says cannot be shown; the REQ-DLV-012 clause (l.35) still counts F-DG7-960's and F-DG7-920's hits as DG7 C3 hits. D-282 is in decisions.md, which ships only in the archive's source/ tree, not in the handover or the register a reader uses. Still Low and non-mandatory, no product behaviour affected; I do not consider it blocking on its own. The minimal repair is a register-note and release-notes wording change by the analyst (REQ-DLV-012, REQ-DLV-014 clauses naming this branch's findings, the other citations qualified as old-branch records), or an ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION decision taken through the protocol (reporting specialist and release-auditor). This assignment allows me only CLOSED_VERIFIED or REOPENED, so I reopen it.
